beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit keys or the full URI to the repo or logs and provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

Use the driver/Mongoose connection options to enable TLS/SSL and set a sensible socket and server selection timeout (e.g. ssl=true, connectTimeoutMS=10000, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=30000) and use the provided connection string verbatim (mongodb:// or mongodb+srv) so driver-level TLS and SRV handling are correct.

Configure a connection pool sized to the workload (set maxPoolSize in the connection options/Mongoose to a value tied to app concurrency, e.g. 50–200) rather than opening many short-lived connections per request.

Treat the canonical customer document as the unit of atomicity and perform single-document upserts (updateOne with upsert:true and targeted $set of nested fields) rather than multi-document transactions; this keeps updates atomic and avoids cross-partition transaction costs.

Use a stable customerId as the unique identifier and create a unique index on customerId (e.g. { customerId: 1 } with unique:true) so upserts use a stable query and you enforce uniqueness at the DB level.

Model each source system as a nested subdocument (e.g. sources.crm, sources.ecomm) and update only the changed sub-paths using $set (e.g. {$set: {'sources.crm.lastSeen': ..., 'sources.crm.attrs.foo': ...}}) to avoid accidentally overwriting other source data.

Make updates idempotent by carrying an eventId or eventSequence per incoming event and recording the last-applied eventId per source in the profile document so duplicate deliveries can be detected and ignored.

Implement retry with exponential backoff for transient errors and for 429 (throttling) responses; detect transient network errors and the provider’s throttling responses and retry with jitter, limiting number of attempts.

Avoid unbounded document growth: cap the size of nested arrays or move high-cardinality/time-series data (events) into a separate collection; ensure profile documents stay well below provider document-size limits (verify actual limit and keep a safe margin).

Create indexes that match read/query patterns (e.g., index customerId plus lastUpdated for queries that fetch recently changed profiles) and avoid creating broad wildcard indexes over large nested subdocuments that inflate RU costs.

When adding or changing indexes, perform idempotent index creation (createIndexes) and avoid changing existing index types in-place; run index creations in an idempotent, offline-safe way (or during low-traffic windows) because some index builds may be expensive.

If you need text or vector search, create a dedicated field for embeddings and add a vector index with explicit index parameters (metricType: 'cosine' or 'euclidean', dims: <vector length>, algorithm_config e.g. {hnsw: {m:16, efConstruction:200}}) and limit vector dimensionality to what the engine and RU budget support.
Use partial or sparse indexes for fields that are only present for some sources (e.g. partialFilterExpression: { 'sources.crm.someField': { $exists: true } }) to reduce index size and RU costs.

Log slow queries, index misses and server selection errors; capture and surface the query patterns (e.g., which predicates are used) so you can iteratively add targeted indexes rather than indexing everything up front.

Reserve a modest, predictable RU/s or use autoscale/auto-provisioning for the database/collection to prevent 429 throttling spikes during ingestion; estimate RU consumption of common operations (upsert with small doc, vector search cost, index builds) and provision accordingly.

Protect the cluster by restricting network access (IP firewall rules or VNet) to only application hosts and CI/CD runners, and store secrets in a secure store (Azure Key Vault) rather than environment variables in CI logs.
Prefer single-document atomic operations and denormalized nested fields over multi-collection joins for the canonical profile to keep reads and writes cheap and to avoid cross-partition transactions.

When seeding sample data and running verify scripts against a shared cluster, operate only in the designated database (sample_customer_360_01) and ensure your scripts are idempotent and clean up after themselves; do not modify other databases or collections on the cluster.

Use schema validation (MongoDB JSON Schema validator) on the collection to enforce expected shapes for the canonical profile (required customerId, sources object shape) so bad events don’t silently corrupt documents.

Avoid excessive indexing of large or high-cardinality nested fields (e.g., indexing many nested attribute names) and instead index the small set of queryable fields (customerId, status, lastUpdated, selected source attributes), monitoring RU costs after index creation.
